correctness.rationale: The normalized kernel power series, after Fourier transforming each regular orbit, separates degrees k modulo m. Summing each residue's geometric series for p=1 and its first moment for p=2 gives the displayed A, B and C up to conjugation of C. Distinct nodes at strict unequal radii and the first 2m coefficients give a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix, so the Gram matrix is positive definite. With t=(rs)^m and c=cos(m phi), put D=1+t^2-2tc>0. The Hardy normalized cross modulus squared is 1/D. In Bergman the squared modulus factor is N/D^2, N=a^2+b^2t^2+2abtc>=0, a=k+1>0, b=m-k-1>=0. The derivative numerator 2abtD+4tN is strictly positive, including b=0 and N=0 cases. Thus each pair at c=-1 is a mean-preserving contraction of the corresponding pair at any c>-1. The direct sum of the pairwise doubly stochastic maps proves full majorization; strict convexity is strict for even one nontrivial contraction, here every pair. All plus eigenvalues increase and all minus eigenvalues decrease off the optimum, so the finite global extrema and condition number have the claimed strictness. Negative log and x^(-a) on the positive spectra yield determinant and inverse-trace conclusions. For Hardy, factoring A_k B_k from each block determinant gives (u^2+v^2-2uvc)/(1+u^2v^2-2uvc), and subtracting cross-products against c=-1 gives 2uv(1+c)(1-u^2)(1-v^2); the ratio denominator is nonzero because u<v. This verifies the exact global deficit as well as the spectral statement.
residual_risks: Only finite normalized Gram spectra for two equally sized regular orbits with 0<r<s<1 and exponents 1 and 2 are assessed, not arbitrary interpolation designs or infinite-dimensional sampling operators.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim for this October 27 record is simultaneous full-spectrum majorization with strict extremal and convex consequences for the two normalized kernel powers. The Hardy determinant law and deficit are classical Cauchy-product consequences, not credited as new by themselves. Two distinct November 2 records are substantial later coverage: one includes the exact Hardy determinant law for equal sizes as a special case; the other proves strict Bergman Fourier-block modulus ordering for every integer p>=2, which already implies the p=2 spectral result by fixed-trace block contraction. This mathematical coverage is explicit, but these later-indexed records are not evidence of antecedence to the frozen result. They also do not state the joint Hardy/Bergman full-spectrum comparison. Earlier inspected frame and determinant work does not provide the same angular Gram spectral order. No absolute claim of historical priority is made.
residual_risks: The later-indexed results show mathematical overlap but do not resolve earlier authorship or priority. Full text of The Bergman norm and the Szegő norm was inaccessible. A specialized earlier spectral placement theorem could be missed in bounded searches.

value.rationale: For fixed concentric sampling orbits it is not automatic that raising the lower Gram bound and lowering the upper one, as well as improving determinant and every inverse trace, have a common optimizer. Here strict block comparison gives a stronger ordering for all convex spectral objectives, in both classical kernel geometries. This yields a useful exact design result beyond rederiving the Hardy Cauchy determinant. The two-block spectra also explain why the conditioning optimum is strict.
residual_risks: No global optimum over unconstrained node placements, arbitrary weights or other exponents is claimed in this review.
